The response returns at once, with phone_deletion.status pending while the phone has not answered; Axilio keeps checking for up to 7 days, asking the phone again until it confirms (phone_deletion.next_check_at is the next check), and a phone not yet set up to delete messages (not_default_app) is asked once it can. GET /messages/{message_id} on any of the deleted messages shows where the phone's copy stands, and each message fires message.deleted, then message.phone_deleted or message.phone_delete_failed, as DELETE /messages/{message_id} describes. get.description: Streams an agent run as Server-Sent Events (text/event-stream): the frames of its session's telemetry that belong to the run, the model's text as it streams (model_delta logs), and the run's own events, live as the run runs. Each event's id is its resume cursor, its event name is the frame kind (span or log), and its data is the frame JSON. The run's events are logs: run_status (attribute axilio.run.status: running when the run starts on its phone or goes back to running), run_input_required (it paused for a person; the body is the question, with the input request's id, reason, requested_by, response_schema and expires_at as attributes), run_resumed (a person answered; the body is the action), run_result (how it ended on the phone: axilio.ok, axilio.run.output or axilio.run.error, and the summary as the body), and user_message (a person's message reached the run; the body is the message). The stream's last event is a run_status with the run's final status as the run itself has it (completed, failed or cancelled), so a run the caller cancelled ends cancelled. These events are not archived; the run itself has the result. A session started with telemetry off still streams its run's events and the model's text, and nothing else. A new reader (or one whose cursor is older than the live window) first receives the run's archived frames and then the live ones, deduplicated on span id and phase, followed by an event with no data that carries the cursor the replay ended at. Reconnect with the Last-Event-ID header to resume. The model's text is not archived: a reader that reconnects after it left the live window gets the step's answer from the run's steps instead. A comment line is sent every 15 seconds while the stream is idle. The stream closes after the run's final status; a reconnect after the end with nothing left gets 204. A run that has not reached a phone yet streams only comments until it does. Authenticate with the API key header, or open the run's stream_url, which carries a read-only token for the run's session. Org-scoped: another org's run reads as not found. Readers MUST ignore events with an unknown name, unknown fields, and unknown span_type or log_type values.

post.description: Sends a person's message to an agent-mode run. To a run that is running or paused, the run's model reads it before its next step, as a turn from the person running the task, and the run's stream carries it as a user_message event, its body the message, once the run's phone has it. A message never resumes a paused run: answer the pause with :resume. A run holds at most 20 unread messages, and the edge refuses one past that, or one that arrives as the run finishes, which may then never be read or shown. To a run that ended (completed, failed or cancelled) while it still holds its phone (keep_alive_expires_at is in the future), the message starts the run's next turn on the same phone, and the run goes back to queued. Returns the run as it is. A code run, a queued or scheduled run, a run whose hold has ended, or a run whose phone cannot take messages yet is 409; an empty message, or one over 64 KiB, is 400.
